reasons.castle: castles and brings the king to safety

concepts.texto: The number next to the opponent (300, 1320, 1800, 3190…) is its Elo: a measure of playing strength. The higher it is, the better it plays. For reference: ~300 absolute beginner, ~800–1200 you're learning, ~1500 club amateur, ~2000 very strong, ~2500 Grandmaster and ~2800+ world champions. The level you choose here sets that number, and with it Stockfish's strength.
Win by delivering checkmate: attack the enemy king so that it cannot escape. The king is never captured; it is cornered. You can also win if the opponent resigns.

Check: the king is under attack and you must save it on the next move. Checkmate: it is under attack and there is no way to save it (end of the game). Draw (tie): for example stalemate (you are not in check but have no legal move), by repetition of the position, or by insufficient material to deliver mate.

Castling: the king and a rook move at the same time to bring the king to safety. En passant capture: a pawn can capture another that has just advanced two squares and ended up beside it. Promotion: a pawn that reaches the last rank is transformed into another piece (almost always a queen).

It helps you decide whether a trade is worth it: pawn 1, knight 3, bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9. The king has no numeric value because it is the objective. The green +N on the bars is the difference in captured material.

Control the center with your pawns; bring out knights and bishops early (develop); castle to protect your king; don't bring out your queen too soon; and before each move ask yourself: “is any of my pieces in danger?”. Turn on coach mode to see the recommended move.

p.mueve: Advances one square in a straight line (or two on its first move) and captures diagonally, never straight ahead. It has two special moves: the en passant capture and promotion.
p.historia: It represents the infantry. It is the only piece that cannot move backward. If it reaches the last rank, it "promotes" and transforms into the piece you choose: a simple pawn can become a queen!
p.objetivos: Control the center and form pawn chains. A "passed pawn" (with no enemy pawns to stop it) can decide the game by racing to promote.

n.mueve: Jumps in an "L" shape: two squares in one direction and one perpendicular. It is the only piece that jumps over others.
n.historia: It represents the cavalry. Its jump makes it unpredictable: it can attack two pieces at once with a "fork". It shines in closed positions where long-range pieces are cramped.
n.objetivos: Look for strong squares near the center where no pawn can drive it away. A well-placed knight in enemy territory is worth its weight in gold.

b.mueve: Slides diagonally any number of squares. Each bishop always lives on squares of a single color.
b.historia: Its Spanish name comes from the Arabic "al-fil", meaning "the elephant". Keeping both bishops (the "bishop pair") is a prized advantage, especially in open positions.
b.objetivos: Open long diagonals and aim at the enemy king. The two bishops complement each other, each covering one color.

r.mueve: Moves in a straight line, horizontally or vertically, any number of squares. It takes part in castling with the king.
r.historia: It represents a war chariot or a siege tower. It is a "heavy" piece that unleashes its full power when the board opens up, in the endgame.
r.objetivos: Dominate open files and place it on the seventh rank, where it traps pawns. Two connected rooks are devastating.

q.mueve: The most powerful piece: it combines the rook and the bishop. It slides straight and diagonally any number of squares.
q.historia: At first it was weak (a "vizier" that moved a single square). In 15th-century Europe it became so strong that this variant was called "mad queen chess".
q.objetivos: Don't bring it out too soon or the opponent will gain time chasing it. Coordinated with other pieces, it is lethal in attack.

k.mueve: Moves a single square in any direction. It has a special move alongside the rook: castling, which brings it to safety.
k.historia: It is the heart of the game: the game ends when the king cannot escape check (checkmate). It is never captured; it is cornered.
k.objetivos: In the opening, bring it to safety (usually by castling). In the endgame, with few pieces, it becomes an active piece that helps promote pawns.

meta.title: VEXCHESS · Chess with AI (Stockfish 18 · NNUE)
meta.description: Chess against a top-tier AI (Stockfish 18 · NNUE) right in your browser. Coach mode, pieces-in-danger warnings, puzzles and an interactive guide. Free and offline.

hero.title:
Think. Play.
Win.
hero.sub: Chess against a top-tier artificial intelligence, with coach mode, pieces-in-danger warnings and an interactive guide to every piece. No servers, no sign-up, right in your browser.

features.heading: Everything you need to improve
features.subtitle: A complete chess experience that runs entirely in your browser.

neural.title: Neural network opponent
neural.body: Stockfish 18 with NNUE evaluation, the strongest open-source engine in the world. Adjustable difficulty from ~1320 to unstoppable strength.

coach.title: Coach mode
coach.body: A second instance of the engine at maximum strength suggests the best move with an arrow and explains why.

danger.title: Pieces-in-danger warning
danger.body: It highlights threatened pieces with a glow and warns you especially when your queen is in danger. Never hang a piece unknowingly again.

guide.title: Interactive guide
guide.body: A large card for each piece with its value, its history and a looping simulation of how it moves and captures.

multilang.title: Multi-language
multilang.body: Spanish and English with automatic detection. The entire interface and guide are translated.

local.title: 100% in your browser
local.body: The engine is compiled to WebAssembly and runs locally. No servers, no API keys, no cost, and it works offline.

ia.heading: Stockfish 18 with NNUE neural network
ia.body: The opponent uses the same engine as Chess.com: Stockfish 18, with neural network evaluation (Efficiently Updatable Neural Network), compiled to WebAssembly and running entirely inside your browser in a Web Worker. It speaks the UCI protocol, thinks in milliseconds and sends nothing to any server.

list.rules: Complete rules via chess.js: castling, promotion, en passant, checkmate and draws.
list.difficulty: Difficulty by Elo or maximum strength, configurable in every game.
list.private: Private by design: all computation happens on your device.

kael.title: The First Move
kael.quote: The board doesn't awaken until someone dares to move.
kael.desc: Kael was the first piece to leave its square when the board was still empty. He serves no rider: he is the impulse that turns a still position into a game. The star on his chest lights up every time someone takes the initiative without yet knowing the outcome.
kael.personality: Brave, direct, restless and contagiously competitive.

aurelia.title: The Silent Crown
aurelia.quote: The strongest move doesn't need to be announced.
aurelia.desc: Aurelia contemplates the board with her eyes closed because she claims the pieces reveal more when they aren't watched. Her golden fragments orbit every possibility and stop only when a perfect sequence exists. She never celebrates a checkmate; for her, the game ended long before.
aurelia.personality: Serene, elegant, demanding and utterly certain.

bastion.title: The Last Wall
bastion.quote: As long as one line stays united, no one is alone.
bastion.desc: Bastion awoke as an isolated rook, but discovered he could link his nodes with every fortress on the board. His barriers don't just protect squares: they create safe routes between allies. When every defense falls, his network keeps the last line lit.
bastion.personality: Loyal, technical, protective and a bit too literal.

nyra.title: The Veiled Diagonal
nyra.quote: I was never in front of you. I was in the angle you forgot.
nyra.desc: Nyra walks along a diagonal set between the visible board and its reflection. The luminous slit of her mask lets her cross both surfaces and appear where a line seemed blocked. No one knows her face, perhaps because beneath the mask there is only another diagonal.
nyra.personality: Reserved, precise, ironic and hard to surprise.

pip.title: The First Square
pip.quote: The whole board fits ahead of a first square.
pip.desc: Pip hasn't reached the last rank yet, and is in no hurry to do so. He wants to know every square, every opponent and every possible way to advance. His little star appears when he finds a new route; that's why he's often the first to enter places that important pieces consider insignificant.
pip.personality: Curious, optimistic, persevering and braver than he thinks.

ordan.title: The Eternal King
ordan.quote: Eternity is about finding one more square.
ordan.desc: Ordan remembers endgames played before clocks existed. The constellations of his crown represent checks he managed to escape, not victories. His power comes not from conquering the board, but from understanding that even a king must bow to the right position.
ordan.personality: Wise, stern, patient and protective of new players.

noctis.title: The Black Fork
noctis.quote: If you can see me, you're already defending the wrong piece.
noctis.desc: Noctis doesn't pass through darkness: he splits it. Each jump leaves two shadows attacking different targets, while his true body remains on the one square no one was watching. His cyan eye calculates the exact instant a threat becomes two.
noctis.personality: Silent, cunning, independent and fiercely precise.

eira-vhal.title: Rivals of the Nexus
eira-vhal.quote: We don't race to defeat each other. We race to discover who we'll be when we arrive.
eira-vhal.desc: Eira was born of the board's light and Vhal of the storm that appeared in its reflection. They both chase the same golden nexus along opposite paths. They've tied so many times that their rivalry became friendship, though neither would agree to say that word in front of the other.
eira-vhal.personality: Eira is disciplined and serene; Vhal, impulsive and proud. Together they're inseparable.

rhazek.title: The Crimson Gambit
rhazek.quote: A piece is a small price for the whole board.
rhazek.desc: Rhazek never looks for a safe square. He was born from the first piece sacrificed voluntarily and learned that an apparent defeat can open the only path to victory. His armor keeps the mark of every gambit no one dared to accept.
rhazek.personality: Bold, provocative, brilliant and dangerously impatient.

oryn.title: Guardian of the Last File
oryn.quote: Every game leaves a truth on the last file.
oryn.desc: Oryn guards the archive of forgotten games. His ribbons contain positions that no longer exist and his rooks store decisions no player recalls having made. When a file is left open, he is the one who decides whether it leads to victory or to the void.
oryn.personality: Solemn, patient, impartial and obsessed with preserving every move.

vesra.title: Queen of the Zugzwang
vesra.quote: You can choose any move. They all belong to me.
vesra.desc: Vesra doesn't immobilize her enemies: she grants them possibilities. Each alternative is part of a network calculated long before the game begins. Her spectral hands don't move pieces; they remove the exits that were never real.
vesra.personality: Serene, majestic, cerebral and unsettlingly courteous.

brakkon.title: The Living Fortress
brakkon.quote: Let the whole kingdom advance. I'll still be here.
brakkon.desc: Brakkon doesn't inhabit a fortress: he is the fortress. He awoke when an entire kingdom took refuge behind the last rook left standing. Each impact adds a new stone to his walls and each protected ally feeds the core that burns beneath his battlements.
brakkon.personality: Protective, silent, loyal and utterly immovable.

ilyra.title: Bishop of Crystal
ilyra.quote: One diagonal is enough when the light finds the right angle.
ilyra.desc: Ilyra contemplates the board as a structure of light. She can traverse long diagonals, split a threat into harmless reflections and uncover lines invisible to others. Every crack in her body holds the memory of a perfect calculation.
ilyra.personality: Precise, distant, curious and surprisingly compassionate.

tikk.title: The Clock Runner
tikk.quote: I don't need more time. I only need your last second.
tikk.desc: Tikk was built to press a clock, but decided to run before anyone could wind him up. He crosses frozen positions, steals lost instants and always reaches the eighth rank a fraction before the impossible. No one knows whether the huge clock on his back is broken or simply running ahead.
tikk.personality: Mischievous, fast, optimistic and fiercely competitive.

malrec.title: The King Without a Crown
malrec.quote: A kingdom may fall. The king must still move.
malrec.desc: Malrec lost his army, his throne and even the right to wear a full crown. He kept only an ivory pawn and the duty to keep it alive. The chains he drags are made of the squares of his former kingdom; each one recalls a retreat he refused to call a defeat.
malrec.personality: Austere, melancholic, strategic and far more dangerous than he appears.

solenne.title: The Eighth Step
solenne.quote: I wasn't born with a crown. I crossed the board to earn it.
solenne.desc: Solenne began as the smallest piece in an anonymous rank. She advanced one square at a time, survived seven impossible lines and reached the far end without forgetting where she came from. Her transformation never ends: the pawn base remains visible beneath a crown built step by step.
